newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM palladium surges, platinum off early highs.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM palladium surges, platinum off early highs.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo palladium futures hung onto early gains and closed up by the daily 22 yen per gram limit across the board, while platinum futures shed some of their early gains but ended firmer, traders said.
Uncertainty over the fate of Russia-Japan talks on platinum group metals for 1997, combined with a possible strike at Russian producer Norilsk, continued to boost platinum group metals, they said.
Benchmark February palladium skyrocketed by 22 yen per gram to 590 yen. Platinum futures ranged from 14 to 40 yen per gram higher, with benchmark February up 20 yen at 1,509 yen.

"Concern over Russian supplies fuelled heavy trading in platinum group metals. Unless the timing of the Japan-Russian talks is decided, platinum group metals could rise further in volatile trading," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
In platinum futures, private investors who were buying earlier, turned to selling to take profits, the traders said.
Daily volume in platinum futures hit a record high of around 177,819 lots on Friday, the highest level in the past.
Gold futures also ended higher in line with platinum group metals. Gold prices ranged from three to 16 yen per gram higher, with benchmark February up 15 yen at 1,388 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $360.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $358.90/359.40 in New York on Thursday.
Traders said the widening spread between gold futures and platinum futures encouraged gold buying while selling platinum, especially late in the day.
Spot platinum fell to $396.50/397.50 at the Tokyo close, after rising to a high of $407.00/408.00 during Asian hours.
Silver futures were mostly weaker in lacklustre trade. Benchmark February was down 0.6 yen per 10 grams at 205.7 yen.
